chunks.title: Hardcoded Credentials & Sensitive Cloud Secret Exposure — Overview & Threat Definition
chunks.text:
VULNERABILITY STANDARD: Hardcoded Credentials & Sensitive Cloud Secret Exposure
Category: Sensitive Data Exposure | Severity: CRITICAL
Identifiers: CWE-798 | OWASP-A02:2021 - Cryptographic Failures
Core Analysis:
CWE-798: Use of Hard-coded Credentials. The software contains hard-coded credentials, such as a password, cryptographic key, AWS Access Key ID, secret key, or private token, which are used for authentication or inbound/outbound authorization. Hardcoded cloud secrets in source repositories or distributed configurations allow unauthorized actors to hijack cloud infrastructure, access sensitive databases, and escalate privileges across cloud tenants without multi-factor authentication.

metadata.doc_title: Hardcoded Credentials & Sensitive Cloud Secret Exposure

chunks.title: Hardcoded Credentials & Sensitive Cloud Secret Exposure — Step-by-Step Remediation
chunks.text:
REMEDIATION & HARDENING GUIDANCE FOR Hardcoded Credentials & Sensitive Cloud Secret Exposure (CWE-798):
Recommended Engineering Actions:
1. Immediately invalidate and rotate all exposed API tokens, AWS Access Keys, and database credentials in the cloud provider IAM console.
2. Migrate hardcoded secrets to an encrypted secret management vault (e.g. AWS Secrets Manager, HashiCorp Vault, Azure Key Vault).
3. Enforce automated pre-commit hooks (e.g. git-secrets, detect-secrets, TruffleHog) to prevent future secret commits.
4. Verify that environment manifests and credentials files (.env, credentials.json, id_rsa) are listed in .gitignore.
Compliance & Reference Standards: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/798.html, https://owasp.org/Top10/A02_2021-Cryptographic_Failures/, https://docs.aws.amazon.com/general/latest/gr/aws-access-keys-best-practices.html

chunks.title: SQL Injection (SQLi) Prevention and Parameterized Query Architecture — Overview & Threat Definition
chunks.text:
VULNERABILITY STANDARD: SQL Injection (SQLi) Prevention and Parameterized Query Architecture
Category: Injection | Severity: CRITICAL
Identifiers: CWE-89 | OWASP-A03:2021 - Injection
Core Analysis:
CWE-89: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements in SQL Command (SQL Injection). The application constructs dynamic database queries by directly concatenating user-controlled input into SQL strings without parameter binding. An attacker can craft malicious inputs containing quotes, boolean conditions, or UNION operators to bypass authentication, dump entire database tables, modify records, or execute administrative stored procedures.

metadata.doc_title: SQL Injection (SQLi) Prevention and Parameterized Query Architecture

chunks.title: SQL Injection (SQLi) Prevention and Parameterized Query Architecture — Step-by-Step Remediation
chunks.text:
REMEDIATION & HARDENING GUIDANCE FOR SQL Injection (SQLi) Prevention and Parameterized Query Architecture (CWE-89):
Recommended Engineering Actions:
1. Use parameterized SQL queries and prepared statements exclusively for all database interactions.
2. Leverage modern ORM layers (such as SQLAlchemy, Hibernate, or Prisma) with bound query variables.
3. Apply the principle of least privilege to database service accounts, restricting DROP, ALTER, and cross-schema access.
4. Implement automated input validation and centralized typing controls before query dispatch.
Compliance & Reference Standards: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/89.html, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/SQL_Injection_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html

chunks.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) & Broken Object Level Authorization — Overview & Threat Definition
chunks.text:
VULNERABILITY STANDARD: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) & Broken Object Level Authorization
Category: Broken Access Control | Severity: HIGH
Identifiers: CWE-639 | OWASP-A01:2021 - Broken Access Control
Core Analysis:
CWE-639: Authorization Bypass Through User-Controlled Key (IDOR / BOLA). The system accesses internal resources using user-supplied identifiers (such as record IDs in URLs or request bodies) without verifying whether the authenticated user has legitimate authorization to access that specific entity. This permits horizontal privilege escalation where User A retrieves private data belonging to User B.

metadata.doc_title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) & Broken Object Level Authorization

chunks.title: Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) & Broken Object Level Authorization — Step-by-Step Remediation
chunks.text:
REMEDIATION & HARDENING GUIDANCE FOR Insecure Direct Object Reference (IDOR) & Broken Object Level Authorization (CWE-639):
Recommended Engineering Actions:
1. Enforce strict server-side tenant ownership validation on every entity query: filter(Record.id == id, Record.owner_id == user.id).
2. Replace sequential integer identifiers with non-enumerable cryptographic UUIDv4 tokens.
3. Implement declarative authorization guards or middleware checks before executing business logic.
4. Perform automated multi-tenant authorization unit and integration testing.
Compliance & Reference Standards: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/639.html, https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa1-broken-object-level-authorization/

chunks.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Mitigation & Context-Aware Output Encoding — Overview & Threat Definition
chunks.text:
VULNERABILITY STANDARD: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Mitigation & Context-Aware Output Encoding
Category: Input Validation | Severity: HIGH
Identifiers: CWE-79 | OWASP-A03:2021 - Injection
Core Analysis:
CWE-79: Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation (XSS). User-supplied input is embedded in web page output without proper contextual encoding or sanitization, allowing malicious scripts to execute in victim browsers. Reflected, stored, and DOM-based XSS can hijack session cookies, redirect victims to phishing portals, or perform actions on behalf of the user.

metadata.doc_title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Mitigation & Context-Aware Output Encoding

chunks.title: Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Mitigation & Context-Aware Output Encoding — Step-by-Step Remediation
chunks.text:
REMEDIATION & HARDENING GUIDANCE FOR Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) Mitigation & Context-Aware Output Encoding (CWE-79):
Recommended Engineering Actions:
1. Apply contextual output encoding (HTML entity encoding, JavaScript variable escaping, URL encoding) prior to DOM insertion.
2. Deploy a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) header: Content-Security-Policy: default-src 'self'; script-src 'self'.
3. Mark session and authentication cookies with the HttpOnly flag to prevent script-based cookie extraction.
4. Utilize modern front-end frameworks (React, Angular, Vue) that escape output variables by default.
Compliance & Reference Standards: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/79.html, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Cross_Site_Scripting_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html

chunks.title: Defensive HTTP Security Response Headers & Edge Gateway Hardening — Overview & Threat Definition
chunks.text:
VULNERABILITY STANDARD: Defensive HTTP Security Response Headers & Edge Gateway Hardening
Category: Security Misconfiguration | Severity: MEDIUM
Identifiers: CWE-16 | OWASP-A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration
Core Analysis:
CWE-16: Configuration Weakness / Missing Defensive Headers. Web applications lacking essential HTTP security response headers expose users to MIME-type sniffing, cross-origin data leakage, and iframe framing attacks. Key headers include Content-Security-Policy, Strict-Transport-Security (HSTS), X-Content-Type-Options, X-Frame-Options, and Referrer-Policy.

metadata.doc_title: Defensive HTTP Security Response Headers & Edge Gateway Hardening

chunks.title: Defensive HTTP Security Response Headers & Edge Gateway Hardening — Step-by-Step Remediation
chunks.text:
REMEDIATION & HARDENING GUIDANCE FOR Defensive HTTP Security Response Headers & Edge Gateway Hardening (CWE-16):
Recommended Engineering Actions:
1. Configure X-Content-Type-Options: nosniff on all static assets and API endpoints to prevent MIME-sniffing exploits.
2. Add X-Frame-Options: DENY or CSP frame-ancestors 'none' to eliminate UI redressing (Clickjacking).
3. Enforce Strict-Transport-Security: max-age=31536000; includeSubDomains; preload across all HTTPS listeners.
4. Set Referrer-Policy: strict-origin-when-cross-origin to protect sensitive query parameters.
Compliance & Reference Standards: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/16.html, https://owasp.org/www-project-secure-headers/

chunks.title: Authentication Architecture & Multi-Factor Security Enforcement — Overview & Threat Definition
chunks.text:
VULNERABILITY STANDARD: Authentication Architecture & Multi-Factor Security Enforcement
Category: Authentication | Severity: HIGH
Identifiers: CWE-306 | OWASP-A07:2021 - Identification and Authentication Failures
Core Analysis:
CWE-306: Missing Authentication for Critical Function. The application does not verify user identity before permitting access to critical business functions, administrative APIs, or sensitive data exports. Lacking authentication boundaries enables unauthenticated attackers to execute management tasks or exfiltrate core database records.

metadata.doc_title: Authentication Architecture & Multi-Factor Security Enforcement

chunks.title: Authentication Architecture & Multi-Factor Security Enforcement — Step-by-Step Remediation
chunks.text:
REMEDIATION & HARDENING GUIDANCE FOR Authentication Architecture & Multi-Factor Security Enforcement (CWE-306):
Recommended Engineering Actions:
1. Require authenticated session tokens or cryptographically signed JWTs on every API endpoint by default.
2. Enforce Multi-Factor Authentication (MFA / WebAuthn) for privileged and administrative portals.
3. Implement centralized authentication middleware that denies unauthenticated requests with HTTP 401.
4. Prevent broken object level and function level authorization via granular RBAC/ABAC role checks.
Compliance & Reference Standards: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/306.html, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Authentication_Cheat_Sheet.html

chunks.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Prevention & Network Segmentation — Overview & Threat Definition
chunks.text:
VULNERABILITY STANDARD: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Prevention & Network Segmentation
Category: Network & Server Security | Severity: HIGH
Identifiers: CWE-918 | OWASP-A10:2021 - Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF)
Core Analysis:
CWE-918: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF). The web server fetches a remote resource without validating the user-supplied destination URL. An attacker can force the server to issue requests to internal cloud metadata services (e.g. 169.254.169.254), loopback addresses (127.0.0.1), or private subnet microservices, leaking cloud IAM credentials and internal secrets.

metadata.doc_title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Prevention & Network Segmentation

chunks.title: Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Prevention & Network Segmentation — Step-by-Step Remediation
chunks.text:
REMEDIATION & HARDENING GUIDANCE FOR Server-Side Request Forgery (SSRF) Prevention & Network Segmentation (CWE-918):
Recommended Engineering Actions:
1. Strictly whitelist allowed destination hostnames and protocols (enforce https:// only).
2. Block private IP ranges (RFC 1918, 127.0.0.0/8, 169.254.169.254) at both DNS resolution and network firewall layers.
3. Disable HTTP redirection following in backend HTTP client libraries.
4. Deploy IMDSv2 with token hops restricted to 1 on AWS cloud instances.
Compliance & Reference Standards: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/918.html, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/Server_Side_Request_Forgery_Prevention_Cheat_Sheet.html

chunks.title: CWE-200: Public Exposure of API Schema & Interactive Documentation — Overview & Threat Definition
chunks.text:
VULNERABILITY STANDARD: CWE-200: Public Exposure of API Schema & Interactive Documentation
Category: API Security | Severity: MEDIUM
Identifiers: CWE-200 | OWASP-A05:2021 - Security Misconfiguration
Core Analysis:
CWE-200: Exposure of Sensitive Information to an Unauthorized Actor. Public exposure of interactive API schema definitions and documentation (e.g., /openapi.json, /docs, /swagger.json, /redoc) discloses internal route structures, parameter types, authentication schemes, and API operations to unauthenticated external actors. How public API schemas aid reconnaissance: While interactive documentation aids legitimate client integration, unrestricted public access provides external attackers with comprehensive blueprints for automated reconnaissance, endpoint discovery, and targeted boundary fuzzing without requiring prior reconnaissance. Important Context: Exposure of API documentation or OpenAPI schemas is an informational exposure weakness and is NOT automatically proof of unauthorized API access, broken object level authorization, or confirmed backend data breach. Actual real-world impact depends strictly on whether sensitive internal endpoints, administrative operations, deprecated parameters, or proprietary operational data structures are disclosed in the published schema.

metadata.doc_title: CWE-200: Public Exposure of API Schema & Interactive Documentation

chunks.title: CWE-200: Public Exposure of API Schema & Interactive Documentation — Step-by-Step Remediation
chunks.text:
REMEDIATION & HARDENING GUIDANCE FOR CWE-200: Public Exposure of API Schema & Interactive Documentation (CWE-200):
Recommended Engineering Actions:
1. Restrict or disable interactive API documentation (/docs, /redoc, /openapi.json) in production environments unless explicitly required for public third-party APIs.
2. Protect sensitive schema and documentation routes with reverse proxy access controls, API gateway authentication, or IP whitelisting.
3. Remove internal, administrative, debug, and deprecated endpoints from publicly accessible schema definitions using schema filters or route tags.
4. Validate that public documentation schemas do not expose internal backend architecture, proprietary data models, or sensitive operational details.
Compliance & Reference Standards: https://cwe.mitre.org/data/definitions/200.html, https://owasp.org/API-Security/editions/2023/en/0xa8-security-misconfiguration/, https://cheatsheetseries.owasp.org/cheatsheets/REST_Security_Cheat_Sheet.html

metadata.doc_title: CWE-200: Public Exposure of API Schema & Interactive Documentation

chunks.title: CWE-200: Public Exposure of API Schema & Interactive Documentation — Technical Verification & Validation
chunks.text:

Recommended Probe Command: curl -k -s -o /dev/null -w "HTTP %{http_code}\n" "https://<target>/openapi.json" (Expect HTTP 401/403/404 on production deployments)
Ensure boundary validation returns appropriate defensive status codes (e.g. 401/403 for access control, clean parameterized failure without error disclosure for injection flaws, or 401/403/404 for protected documentation endpoints).

1. Disable interactive API documentation endpoints (/docs, /openapi.json, /swagger) in production environments.
2. Enforce authentication and role-based access control on sensitive schema endpoints.
3. Filter API schemas to exclude internal, administrative, or deprecated routes.
